A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoBridge and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices. Corresponding content can be matched reliably across renaming and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation and real-world manipulation experiments, ablations and qualitative analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds a baseline comparison, component ablations and expert-training results.

M1.justification: The HCP–IOR–GEA architecture, representations, closed-loop control and adaptive DAgger procedure remain unchanged. Renaming GEA from Generalist to Guided and adding ablation variants do not establish changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MetaWorld and Robosuite tasks, environmental perturbations, unseen tasks, real-world manipulation tasks and long-horizon sequence. The additions use retained task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds RAM to the real-world comparison; v1 cited RAM but did not evaluate it there. The comparator sets in Tables 1, 3, 4 and 7 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 5 adds evaluation configurations using keypoints, language-only input and a smaller VLM. Existing splits, training budgets and evaluation conditions remain unchanged; the smaller VLM's identity and size are unspecified.

E4.justification: Table 5 substantially extends component analysis to alternative symbolic interfaces and planner capacity through three new ablations. Appendix B.2 and Figure 5 add expert-training convergence diagnostics. The earlier failure-recovery and DINOv2 analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both Table 8 captions specify ten tests per task. Neither version reports training-seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests, and the added learning curves provide no uncertainty bands.

E6.justification: Existing scores remain unchanged. Additions include RAM's 44.17% mean in Table 2; keypoint, language-only and smaller-VLM means of 59.88%, 39.28% and 63.84% in Table 5; and expert-training curves with a reported 90.8% success rate in Appendix B.2. These supplement retained results rather than demonstrate improved same-setting performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical representation in Equation 1 and the associated definitions remain unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the architecture, robustness and generalization claims, including 75% success on unseen tasks and approximately 83% real-world success. The added holistic-system sentence elaborates the existing integration claim.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 newly interprets the controls as evidence that IOR helps beyond richer supervision and that VLM capability matters for understanding instructions and images. Appendix A's limitations are unchanged; the failure explanation moves from Section 4.6 to Appendix C.3.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds A100 hardware, 25/30 GPU-hour expert/GEA training costs, one GPU-hour fine-tuning, 6 GB inference memory excluding GPT-4o, and module invocation and latency details. These are new disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to existing training settings.

R1.justification: The introduction explicitly acknowledges prior contributions to individual ingredients and emphasizes integrated-system novelty; Section 4.2 adds a description of RAM. The additional Pivot-R bibliography entry duplicates an already cited work rather than expanding literature coverage.

P1.justification: v3 consistently renames Generalist Embodied Agent to Guided Embodied Agent, adds short explanatory passages, updates affiliations and acknowledgements, and relocates failure analysis to Appendix C.3. Most prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 5 gain rows, and a new RL training plot becomes Figure 5. The original failure-recovery Figure 5 moves to the appendix as Figure 8, while Table 8 moves to the final page. Other displays retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The added RAM comparison, representation/VLM ablations and training diagnostics strengthen empirical support, while Appendix B.2 makes computational requirements more transparent. The gain is limited because the new ablation implementations, especially the smaller VLM, remain underspecified and uncertainty reporting is unchanged.
